entities.name: La France insoumise
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
La France Insoumise (France Unbowed, LFI), founded in 2016 by Jean-Luc Mélenchon as an anti-establishment left-wing party after his break from the Socialist Party, became France's largest left-wing party by 2022 — winning 142 seats in the National Assembly (second largest party) and making Mélenchon the primary challenger to Emmanuel Macron in the 2022 presidential election, where he came third (21.95%) but nearly edged out Marine Le Pen for the runoff. LFI's emergence displaced the Socialist Party (governing 1997-2002, 2012-2017) as France's dominant left force.

Mélenchon created LFI as a 'France Unbowed' movement — deliberately evoking the language of national sovereignty and resistance to neoliberal economics and EU austerity, while maintaining left-wing economics (wealth taxation, minimum wage increases, public services expansion). LFI's social media strategy (YouTube, Hologram rallies where Mélenchon appeared simultaneously at 7 locations via hologram projection) pioneered digital political communication in France. The 2017 presidential campaign (19.58% in first round) established LFI as a major force.

The 2022 NUPES alliance — LFI leading a left electoral coalition (Socialists, Greens, Communists) for the legislative elections — achieved 142 seats and nearly formed the opposition government. LFI's positions include France's withdrawal from NATO command, renegotiation of EU treaties, and the Sixth Republic (replacing the Fifth Republic's presidential system). The party's anti-Zionism positions have been controversial, with critics alleging antisemitism and supporters defending anti-imperialism.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: La France Insoumise — displacing France's century-old Socialist Party as the dominant left force in 10 years and pioneering hologram political rallies — represents the most complete left-party realignment in French political history since the PS's founding, and a global model for insurgent left digital political campaigns.
